key_insight: CREW replaces fixed multi-agent workflows for related work generation with learned, dynamic coordination among LLM agents.
engineering_relevance: The framework suggests a more adaptive and cost-efficient way to automate literature synthesis for scientific writing tools.
method: LLM agents choose actions autonomously: Retrieve, Disseminate, Compose, Critique.
Agent policies are optimized with Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (IPPO).
Designed to bypass rigid heuristic pipelines and enable collaborative multi-agent reasoning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on a standard RWG benchmark, showing higher quality than strong baselines and lower token cost.
watch_item: Performance may depend on stable policy training and careful agent coordination, which could be sensitive to benchmark/domain shifts.
paper_title: Assembling the CREW: A Collaborative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Automated Related Work Generation
